anomalies.description: A sudden bright flash and rapid expansion of fire and smoke erupts from the lower right portion of a multi-level industrial or construction structure, consistent with an explosion.

Sustained intense fire, structural disintegration, and debris ejection following the initial blast; the scene shows progressive collapse and burning of the structure over several seconds, indicating a post-explosive fire and structural failure event.

A bright flash and rapidly expanding fireball with smoke emanates from a structure at ground level, consistent with a sudden explosive event. The intensity peaks around 10–11 seconds and begins to dissipate by 12.5 seconds.

After the explosion subsides, two individuals in white helmets appear to be engaged in close physical interaction on a platform; however, motion blur and low resolution prevent confirmation of mutual combat versus rescue or post-incident movement.

A sudden, violent explosion occurs at the industrial facility, producing a large white vapor cloud and visible structural disruption near the two spherical tanks.; A second distinct explosion or rapid escalation of the incident occurs on the right side of the facility, marked by a bright flash and emergence of fire and smoke from the multi-story structure.; A third explosive event or major fire intensification is observed, with increased flame size and smoke plume growth from the right-side structure, suggesting propagation or secondary detonation.

A large, sudden fireball erupts from the industrial structure, characteristic of a rapid deflagration or explosion, with intense white-yellow flame and rapid expansion visible in the final frame.; A sudden, massive fireball erupts from the industrial facility, indicating a violent explosion. The blast is instantaneous and fills the frame with intense white-yellow flame and expanding gases.; Sustained post-explosion combustion and secondary detonations or rapid burning follow the initial blast, with large flames engulfing structures and thick black smoke rising. This phase shows continued energetic release consistent with an ongoing explosive event (e.g., BLEVE or fuel-air explosion).

A large, sustained fireball and rapidly expanding plume of black smoke erupt from a ground-level industrial or storage facility, consistent with a fuel or chemical explosion; the fire intensifies and spreads across multiple frames, with visible structural damage and debris.

A large, sudden fireball erupts with intense orange flames and a rapidly expanding plume of black smoke, consistent with a violent explosion involving flammable material (e.g., fuel or gas tanks). The blast appears to originate from a ground-level industrial or transport facility.; A secondary, smaller explosion or deflagration occurs amid the ongoing fire, marked by a bright flash and renewed flame expansion at approximately 36.5–37.0 s, followed by continued intense burning and structural collapse debris visible through the railing.
A sudden, violent burst of fire and smoke erupts from the vehicle structure, consistent with an explosion; bright flash and rapid expansion of debris and flame are visible.

A severely damaged vehicle (likely a bus or large truck) is engulfed in fire and smoke, indicating it has crashed and caught fire; structural deformation and sustained combustion confirm a post-collision fire event.
